name: SettingsList
description: A list of settings, each a title and optional description with a control at the end: a switch, a button or a select. Use it for account and security settings.
whenToUse: For account, security and preference pages with several settings.
When each setting has one control: on/off, or one action such as "Change".

whenNotToUse.text: For key–value details that are not editable.
For a single on/off setting on its own.

anatomy.name: Control
anatomy.description: A Switch, Button or Select at the end of the row.

values.meaning: Default. Rows on the page, divided by lines.

states.name: Static
states.meaning: Rows with their controls; each control has its own states.

behavior.text: Each control keeps its own behaviour: a Switch saves on change, a Button runs its action.
Text sits on the right and controls on the left in Arabic.

content: Title each setting with the thing it controls, e.g. "Two-factor authentication".
Show the current state in the description, e.g. "Last changed 3 months ago".

guidelines.dont: Put several controls in one row.
guidelines.why: One control per row keeps the outcome of each setting clear.

guidelines.do: Use a switch for settings that apply at once.
guidelines.dont: Use a switch for settings that need a Save button.
guidelines.why: A switch implies the change is already saved.

guidelines.do: Describe the current state under the title.
guidelines.dont: Hide the state until the control is opened.
guidelines.why: People should see what is set before they change it.

accessibility.role: list of rows; each control keeps its own role and name.

keyboard.action: Moves through the controls in order.

aria.when: On switches without a visible name in the row.

accessibility.focus: Each control shows its own focus ring.

wcag.how: Rows are list items; the title is read before its control.

notes: Give each switch a name that matches its row title.

examples.title: Security settings
examples.description: A switch, a button and a description.

examples.title: Notification preferences
examples.code:
import { SettingsList, Switch } from '@ds/react';

<SettingsList items={channels.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, title: c.title, control: <Switch aria-label={c.title} checked={c.on} onCheckedChange={(v) => set(c.id, v)} /> }))} />

related.relation: For details that are read, not changed.

components.name: SettingsList
components.description:
A list of settings, each a title and optional description with a control at the end. Use it
for on/off switches and one-off actions in account and security settings.

framed.description: Draws a border around the list, for a settings card.

--settings-list-font-family.description: Body text and most UI text.

--settings-list-text-gap.description: Hairline gap (2px), e.g. between rating stars.

--settings-list-description-color.description: Supporting text on surfaces: descriptions, metadata, placeholders.

--settings-list-framed-padding-x.description: Gap between groups inside a section.

--settings-list-border-radius.description: Controls and small surfaces: inputs, buttons, menu items.
